skill.name: create-new-skills
skill.description: Guides Claude Code through creating reusable Agent Skills with clear triggers, structured instructions, examples, and optional supporting files.
skill.summary: Create well-structured Claude Code Agent Skills from a user workflow or domain need.
skill.author: EGAdams

security_audit.summary: All static findings were adjudicated as false positives caused by documentation examples, Markdown code formatting, and legitimate Claude Code skill path references. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, unauthorized command execution, or hidden malicious behavior was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes destructive shell examples for deleting a skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Add a caution near removal commands advising users to verify the exact path before running deletion commands.

remediation.issue: Several example commands may be copied directly by users.
remediation.suggestion: Keep placeholders obvious and tell users to replace sample names with their own reviewed paths.

content.value_statement: Teams need repeatable ways to package workflows and domain knowledge for AI agents. This skill guides Claude Code through designing, writing, and testing focused Agent Skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains how Agent Skills are structured with SKILL.md frontmatter and Markdown instructions.
Guides users through defining a skill purpose, triggers, and workflow before writing files.
Provides examples for simple skills, script-backed skills, documentation skills, and skill extensions.
Recommends project skill placement for team sharing and personal skill placement for individual use.
Covers testing steps for file structure, frontmatter, and trigger behavior.
limitations: It provides authoring guidance but does not guarantee a skill will trigger in every conversation.
It relies on the user to supply the workflow, domain rules, and validation examples.
It includes documentation examples for shell commands that should be reviewed before use.
It is focused on Claude Code skills, not every skill format across all Claude surfaces.

use_cases.title: Package a team workflow
use_cases.description: Turn a repeatable engineering workflow into a shared project skill with clear triggers and instructions.

use_cases.title: Create a personal productivity skill
use_cases.description: Capture an individual workflow as a personal Claude Code skill with examples and supporting references.

use_cases.title: Design a script-backed skill
use_cases.description: Plan a skill that includes helper scripts, templates, or supporting documentation using progressive disclosure.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new skill from a short idea.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code skill for reviewing Python code style. Ask me any missing questions before writing it.

prompt_templates.title: Turn a workflow into a skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Convert a known process into reusable instructions.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project skill from this workflow: first inspect changed files, then run tests, then summarize release risk.

prompt_templates.title: Add supporting files
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a richer skill with references or templates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a documentation skill that uses a style guide, an API template, and examples as supporting files.

prompt_templates.title: Extend an existing skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced update to an existing skill package.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update our existing transcribe skill so it applies project-specific spelling corrections from a separate reference file.

output_examples.input: Create a skill that reviews Python code for best practices.
output_examples.output: Claude asks clarifying questions, creates a focused skill structure, drafts SKILL.md, and suggests tests for trigger behavior.

output_examples.input: Build a CSV analysis skill with charts and a report template.
output_examples.output: Claude proposes a skill directory with scripts and templates, then writes instructions for when to run each helper.

output_examples.input: Add spell correction to our existing transcribe skill.
output_examples.output: Claude reads the current skill, adds a supporting correction file, updates the workflow, and recommends a test case.

best_practices: Define the skill trigger and user goal before writing files.
Keep the main SKILL.md focused and move detailed references into supporting files.
Test the skill with realistic user requests after creating or changing it.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated workflows into one broad skill.
Do not use vague descriptions that make skill activation unreliable.
Do not add scripts or shell commands unless the user needs executable automation.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code Agent Skills with SKILL.md instructions, examples, and optional supporting files.

faq.question: Can it create skills for a team?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends project skill locations when the skill should be shared through a repository.

faq.question: Can it create personal skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains personal skill placement for workflows that should not be shared with a project.

faq.question: Does it write executable scripts?
faq.answer: It can guide script-backed skills when needed, but scripts should be reviewed before use.

faq.question: Does it test created skills automatically?
faq.answer: It provides testing steps and can help run checks when the user asks Claude Code to perform them.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, with primary guidance for Claude Code.
